title: 随机性的数学 · Day 37 — Mathematics
title_en: The Mathematics of Randomness · Day 37 — Mathematics

questions.question: 一维随机游走每步等概率向左或向右走一格。走了 10000 步之后，离起点的典型距离大约是多少？
options: 约 0 步，因为左右各半，正负会相互抵消
约 100 步：抵消的是方向不是距离，典型距离按步数的平方根增长
约 5000 步，因为平均只有一半的步子朝同一方向推进，另一半恰好互相抵消
约 10000 步，因为每一步都让你离开上一个位置
questions.explanation: 期望位置确实是 0，但 E[S_n²]=n，典型偏移是 √n：100 步约 10 步，10000 步约 100 步。「正负抵消回到原地」的直觉错在把方向的抵消当成了距离的抵消；径直走才是 n。
questions.question_en: In a one-dimensional random walk, each step goes left or right with equal probability. After 10,000 steps, roughly how far from the start is the walker typically?
options_en: About 0 steps, since left and right moves cancel out
About 100 steps: what cancels is direction, not distance, and typical distance grows like the square root of the step count
About 5,000 steps, since on average half the steps push in one direction while the other half cancel out
About 10,000 steps, since every step moves you away from where you were
questions.explanation_en: The expected position is 0, but E[S_n²] = n, so the typical displacement is √n: about 10 after 100 steps, about 100 after 10,000. The "it all cancels" intuition confuses cancellation of direction with cancellation of distance; walking straight would give n.

questions.question: 「鞅」作为公平赌局的数学定义，准确的含义是什么？
options: 每一轮输赢的概率相同，所以长期下来赌本一定回到初始值
赌本的数值始终保持不变，不会出现大的波动
只要采用合适的停止规则，比如输了就加倍下注、赢一次就收手，就能保证期望收益为正
给定全部历史，对下一轮赌本的最优预测就是当前值，历史里没有可利用的方向
questions.explanation: 鞅说的不是值不变——波动可以大到破产——而是趋势为零：E[X_{n+1}|F_n]=X_n。可选停时定理进一步说明，只要不能预知未来、下注受限，任何停止规则都改不了期望；倍投法几乎必然赢一块，代价是小概率连败里输掉天文数字，期望恰好抹平。
questions.question_en: What exactly does a martingale—the mathematical definition of a fair game—mean?
options_en: Each round has equal odds of winning and losing, so the bankroll always returns to its starting value in the long run
The bankroll's value stays constant and never fluctuates much
With the right stopping rule—say, double after every loss and quit after one win—expected profit can be made positive
Given all the history so far, the best prediction of next round's bankroll is its current value; history holds no exploitable directional information
questions.explanation_en: A martingale doesn't mean the value stays put—swings can be large enough to ruin you—it means zero drift: E[X_{n+1}|F_n] = X_n. The optional stopping theorem adds that, without foresight and with bounded bets, no stopping rule changes the expectation; doubling almost surely wins one unit but loses astronomically in the rare losing streak, exactly cancelling out.

questions.question: 把一个 1000×1000 对称矩阵的每个元素都填上独立随机数，再求它的特征值，会看到什么？
options: 特征值稳定地落在一条半圆曲线下，换一批随机数也不变，且彼此排斥、均匀排开
只有维度很低时才会出现规律；维度越高，随机叠加越多，特征值就越接近均匀铺满整条实轴
特征值杂乱无章，每换一批随机数分布形状都完全不同
特征值像独立撒下的随机点一样成团扎堆，集中在零附近
questions.explanation: 这是 Wigner 半圆律：单个元素彻底无序，整体谱却是刚性的秩序，波动以 1/N 的量级消失，维度把随机熨平。特征值之间还相互排斥，不像独立随机点那样扎堆。高维反而让宏观量更可预测，这是测度集中的一种面孔。
questions.question_en: Fill every entry of a symmetric 1000×1000 matrix with independent random numbers and compute its eigenvalues. What do you see?
options_en: The eigenvalues fall reliably under a semicircle that stays put with fresh random numbers, and they repel each other, spreading evenly
Patterns appear only in low dimensions; the higher the dimension, the more randomness piles up and the closer eigenvalues come to covering the real line uniformly
The eigenvalues are chaotic, and their distribution changes shape completely with each new batch of random numbers
The eigenvalues clump together near zero, like independently scattered random points
questions.explanation_en: This is Wigner's semicircle law: each entry is pure disorder, yet the spectrum as a whole is rigidly ordered, with fluctuations vanishing at order 1/N—dimension irons out the randomness. Eigenvalues also repel one another rather than clumping like independent points. High dimension makes macroscopic quantities more predictable, one face of concentration of measure.
